reading.title: What Suffixes Tell Us About Things and People
reading.purpose: Discover how the suffixes -able, -ible, and -ness describe qualities and feelings.
paras: Word ends called suffixes do quiet work in English. Three useful ones, -able, -ible, and -ness, show what a thing can do or name a state.

The ends -able and -ible mean "can be" or "fit for." A bike hat has an adjustable strap so you can change it to fit snug. If a book is available, it is right on the shelf for you to take home. Dry desert skies can be predictable, easy to guess from day to day. A reversible coat can flip inside out to show a new hue.

Some -ible words fit things in the woods and at home. Young willow limbs are flexible, bending in hard wind without snapping. A flexible team can shift plans with ease too. Ask a guide before tasting wild berries, since not each bright berry is edible, or safe to eat.

The end -ness names a trait or feeling. Good friends prize fairness, treating each kid the same. A child's willingness to help shows they are glad to pitch in. Growing awareness of how peers feel helps a class spot loneliness and ask a new kid to play.
Spotting -able, -ible, and -ness turns big words into clear ideas.

choices: ready on a shelf to borrow from a library
able to bend in strong wind without breaking
safe for a person to eat
easy to guess before it happens
qs.why: Paragraph 3 states directly that edible means "safe to eat."

qs.q: Which sentence shows what a reversible coat can do?
choices: A bike hat has an adjustable strap so you can change it to fit snug.
If a book is available, it is right on the shelf for you to take home.
A reversible coat can flip inside out to show a new hue.
Spotting -able, -ible, and -ness turns big words into clear ideas.
qs.why: This sentence explains that a reversible coat can flip inside out to show a new hue.

ev.text: A reversible coat can flip inside out to show a new hue.

qs.q: How can awareness help a classroom feel welcoming?
choices: It helps students notice loneliness and invite others to join.
It makes desert weather easier to guess before recess begins.
It lets students flip their rain jackets inside out in the hallway.
It ensures every wild berry near the playground is safe to eat.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says building awareness of how others feel helps a class notice someone's loneliness and invite them to join.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Bicycle helmets and willow trees are the best examples of words ending in -ness.
The suffixes -able, -ible, and -ness show what things can do or name qualities.
Every describing word in English can take both -able and -ible at the same time.
Library books are only available when students show fairness and willingness.
qs.why: The reading explains the meanings of -able, -ible, and -ness through clear everyday examples.
